question: Should autoreview treat credential-shaped member references rooted at the generic JavaScript/TypeScript names `data` and `providerConfig` as safe source references?
rationale: The patch is technically well-tested, but the acceptable breadth of a fail-closed secret-scanner exemption is a repository security-policy choice that automated review should not make.

options.title: Approve the scoped roots
options.body: Accept both names because the exemption is limited to syntactically safe references in per-file JavaScript/TypeScript diff sections and literal-secret controls remain active.

options.title: Narrow the generic root
options.body: Keep `providerConfig` but replace or remove `data` unless the motivating branch proves a more specific stable root cannot solve the false positive.

options.title: Keep the current boundary
options.body: Decline the expansion and leave the linked issue open for a different parser or redaction-based approach.

recommendation.title: Approve the scoped roots
recommendation.body: Accept both names because the exemption is limited to syntactically safe references in per-file JavaScript/TypeScript diff sections and literal-secret controls remain active.
